# The Margins

The first correction appeared on a Tuesday, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been returned through the book drop. Marisol found it while checking the pages for damage—standard practice, since the drop had a habit of swallowing books whole and creasing them in the process.

*Heathcliff would not have said this,* the pencil note read, in small, careful letters beside a line of dialogue. *He would have said nothing at all. He was better at silence.*

Marisol frowned at the graphite, then at the due date. She should have charged the borrower for defacing library property. Instead, she found herself reading the note twice, and then, despite herself, glancing at the passage to see if the stranger had a point.

They did, actually.

The Seaview Public Library sat three blocks up from the harbor, a squat brick building with fog-gray windows and a boiler that groaned like a docked ship. Marisol had been the head librarian for eleven years, ever since she'd moved to Kessler Bay for what was supposed to be one year of quiet after her divorce, and had discovered that quiet was a thing you could build a life around. She knew her patrons by name:
